details: Text-to-music systems built on audio-codec language models or diffusion over spectrogram latents, with controls for style, structure, stems, and vocals. Shares its codec foundations with speech synthesis, and sits in the middle of the training-data licensing storm.

explainer.lead: Music generation covers text-to-music systems built on audio-codec language models or diffusion over spectrogram latents, with controls for style, structure, stems, and vocals. It shares codec foundations with speech synthesis and sits in the middle of the training-data licensing storm.

tiers.eli5: You type 'upbeat lo-fi with a soft piano' and the machine composes a track to match.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers either tokenise audio with a codec and model the tokens with a language model, or run diffusion over spectrogram latents, exposing prompts and controls for style, structure, stems, and vocals. A pitfall is that training data licensing is unresolved, so provenance of generated output is contested.
tiers.paperLevel: Generate audio either autoregressively over discrete codec tokens or by denoising in a latent spectrogram space conditioned on text and control inputs. Control over long-range structure and exact stems remains limited.

explainer.example: A prompt specifying style and a vocal stem yields a short track with separated vocal and instrumental parts.
